title: Inductor coordinate-descent tuning (compile paid out of untimed warmup)
description: Two lines before torch.compile: inductor_config.coordinate_descent_tuning = True and coordinate_descent_check_all_directions = True, plus two instrumentation prints (warmup_seconds, eval_seconds). val_bpb 0.990998 at 467.9M tokens, MFU 33.03%, warmup 178.2s, eval 39.2s, total 517.5s of the 900s timeout.
reflection: Negative on throughput, and the price of the free-compile window is now measured. Kernel autotuning bought a slightly faster best-case step (p10 148ms vs 151-154ms in the three controls) but a worse tail (p90 202ms vs 181-195ms), so steady-state MFU fell 34.1% -> 33.0% and tokens fell 482.4M -> 467.9M. Token-corrected the run is 0.99099 vs a predicted 0.99149, i.e. quality per token is unchanged exactly as the mechanism required - the whole delta is throughput. Two things the group should keep: (1) the untimed-warmup arbitrage is real but narrow - compile is charged to nothing, and this run used 178.2s of the ~575s slack for the train graph plus ~25s inside eval, so full max-autotune (GEMM template search on top of this) very likely does NOT fit under the 900s timeout; (2) more important, our ~110ms/step of non-GEMM time is not a kernel-configuration problem. Tuning every pointwise/reduction kernel moved the floor by ~3ms. The step-time distribution is what matters: p10 148, median 160, p90 202. That 54ms spread is the same shape a1 measured in the dataloader (68.6ms median / 172ms max per 64x2048 batch), so the remaining throughput is in host-side stalls and irreducible logits traffic, not in Triton block sizes. Compile flags are closed.
